concepts.name: Grounds for Proclamation of Financial Emergency
key_dimensions: Exact constitutional language: 'financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened' — distinguishing 'stability' from 'credit'
Subjective satisfaction of the President vs. objective criteria — comparison with Article 356 post-44th Amendment
Whether a financial crisis in a single state can trigger Article 360 ('any part thereof' clause)
Absence of the word 'imminent' — contrast with Article 352 which uses 'imminent danger'

concepts.name: Presidential Satisfaction and Judicial Review of Article 360 Proclamation
key_dimensions: Pre-44th Amendment position: Presidential satisfaction was non-justiciable
Post-44th Amendment and S.R. Bommai implications: Whether 'satisfaction' under Article 360 is now justiciable
Standard of review — malafide, irrelevant grounds, or no material at all
Comparison with Article 352 (National Emergency) and Article 356 (President's Rule) on justiciability

concepts.name: Parliamentary Approval of Financial Emergency Proclamation
key_dimensions: Approval required within two months by both Houses — simple majority (not special majority)
UPSC trap: Article 360 requires simple majority, unlike Article 352 which requires special majority (2/3rd + majority of total membership)
What happens if Lok Sabha is dissolved before approval — no special provision unlike Article 352
Indefinite continuance once approved — no six-month renewal requirement, unlike Article 352

concepts.name: Duration and Continuance of Financial Emergency
key_dimensions: No maximum period specified — continues indefinitely until revoked
No periodic renewal required — sharp contrast with Article 352 (renewable every 6 months) and Article 356 (3-year maximum)
Revocation mechanism: President can revoke at any time without parliamentary approval
UPSC trap: Financial Emergency, once approved, does not lapse automatically — it is the only Emergency with no sunset clause

concepts.name: Revocation of Financial Emergency
key_dimensions: President can revoke by a subsequent proclamation — no parliamentary approval needed for revocation
Contrast with Article 352: Revocation of National Emergency requires Lok Sabha passing a resolution by simple majority
No role of Rajya Sabha or special majority in revocation
UPSC trap: Unlike National Emergency, there is no provision for Lok Sabha to pass a resolution demanding revocation of Financial Emergency

concepts.name: Effect on Salaries and Allowances of Government Servants
key_dimensions: President can direct reduction of salaries and allowances of ALL persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union
Includes judges of Supreme Court and High Courts — a unique and UPSC-favourite feature
Distinction: Reduction of judges' salaries is only possible under Financial Emergency, NOT under ordinary legislation (protection under Article 125 and 221 is overridden)
Contrast with National Emergency which does not directly empower salary reduction of judges

concepts.name: Presidential Directions to States During Financial Emergency
key_dimensions: President can give directions to any State to observe specified canons of financial propriety
President can direct State governments to reduce salaries/allowances of state employees
President can require all Money Bills and Financial Bills passed by State legislature to be reserved for Presidential consideration
UPSC trap: Under Article 360, ALL financial bills of states can be reserved — not just those the Governor chooses to reserve

concepts.name: Reservation of State Money Bills for Presidential Assent
key_dimensions: Under Article 360(4)(b)(ii): President can direct that Money Bills of states be reserved for his consideration
This overrides the normal process where Governor gives assent — Governor's discretion is bypassed
Comparison with ordinary reservation under Article 200 (Governor's discretion) and Article 201 (Presidential assent)
Implication: Centre gains full financial control over State legislation during Financial Emergency

concepts.name: Impact on Federal Structure During Financial Emergency
key_dimensions: Article 360 effectively converts India into a unitary state for financial matters
Centre can give binding directions to States on financial matters — overriding normal federal division
State autonomy in financial legislation (Money Bills) is completely subordinated
Comparison with Article 249, 250, 353 — other provisions that centralise power, but none as comprehensively as Article 360

concepts.name: Canons of Financial Propriety — Meaning and Scope
key_dimensions: Article 360(3): President may give directions regarding 'canons of financial propriety' — term not defined in the Constitution
Interpreted to include sound fiscal management, balanced budgets, avoiding wasteful expenditure
UPSC angle: The phrase is deliberately vague — giving the Centre wide discretion
Comparison with the concept of 'fiscal responsibility' under FRBM Act — statutory vs. constitutional basis

concepts.name: Comparison of Article 360 with Article 352 (National Emergency)
key_dimensions: Grounds: External aggression/armed rebellion (352) vs. threat to financial stability/credit (360)
Parliamentary approval: Special majority (352) vs. Simple majority (360)
Duration: Renewable every 6 months (352) vs. No renewal, indefinite (360)
Revocation: Lok Sabha can demand revocation (352) vs. No such provision (360)

concepts.name: Comparison of Article 360 with Article 356 (President's Rule)
key_dimensions: Article 356 imposes President's Rule on a specific state; Article 360 operates across India or any part
Article 356 has a maximum duration of 3 years; Article 360 has no maximum
Under Article 356, State legislature is suspended/dissolved; under Article 360, State legislature continues but financial bills are controlled
S.R. Bommai safeguards apply strongly to Article 356 but their application to Article 360 is debated

concepts.name: Historical Non-Use of Article 360 and Its Implications
key_dimensions: Article 360 has NEVER been proclaimed in India's constitutional history — a critical UPSC fact
1991 Balance of Payments crisis: Widely debated whether Article 360 should have been invoked — it was not
Implications of non-use: Lack of judicial interpretation, no precedents unlike Articles 352 and 356
Why not used in 1991: Political costs, IMF conditionality, administrative difficulties of Centre controlling all state finances

concepts.name: Role of Cabinet in Advice to President for Article 360
key_dimensions: 44th Amendment introduced written Cabinet advice requirement for Article 352 — does the same apply to Article 360?
Article 360 does not explicitly require written Cabinet advice — a significant UPSC distinction
Article 74(1): Council of Ministers' aid and advice applies generally, but no specific written requirement for Article 360
UPSC trap: Only Article 352 explicitly requires Cabinet's written advice; Article 360 has no such explicit safeguard

concepts.name: Article 360 and Its Relationship with the Consolidated Fund of India
key_dimensions: During Financial Emergency, President can direct reduction of salaries charged to the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI)
Judges' salaries are charged to CFI (not voted) under Articles 125 and 221 — yet Article 360 overrides this protection
UPSC angle: Article 360 is the ONLY mechanism to reduce judges' salaries — not even ordinary Parliament can do so otherwise
Implication for judicial independence: Financial Emergency poses a structural threat to separation of powers

concepts.name: Scope of 'Any Part of the Territory of India' in Article 360
key_dimensions: Article 360(1): Emergency can be declared if financial stability of India OR 'any part thereof' is threatened
This means a regional financial crisis (e.g., one state's insolvency) can trigger a national-level proclamation
UPSC trap: Many students assume Financial Emergency requires a national-level crisis — it does not
Contrast with Article 352 where 'any part of India' being under threat also triggers a national Emergency

concepts.name: Safeguards Against Misuse of Article 360 — Adequacy and Criticism
key_dimensions: Existing safeguards: Parliamentary approval (simple majority), judicial review (limited)
Absent safeguards: No special majority required, no Lok Sabha resolution for revocation, no maximum duration
Criticism: Article 360 is the least safeguarded of the three Emergency provisions — potentially the most prone to misuse
Sarkaria Commission and NCRWC recommendations on strengthening safeguards for Financial Emergency

concepts.name: Financial Emergency and Its Effect on Fundamental Rights
key_dimensions: Unlike National Emergency (Article 352), Financial Emergency does NOT suspend Fundamental Rights
Article 19 rights are NOT automatically suspended during Financial Emergency
UPSC trap: Students often assume all Emergencies affect Fundamental Rights — only National Emergency does so directly
However, reduction of salaries could indirectly affect Article 21 (right to livelihood) — a debated dimension

concepts.name: Role of Parliament During Financial Emergency — Legislative Competence
key_dimensions: Article 360 does NOT expand Parliament's legislative competence (unlike Article 353 under National Emergency)
Parliament cannot legislate on State List subjects merely because Financial Emergency is in force
The Centre's power under Article 360 is executive direction, not legislative expansion
UPSC trap: Conflating Article 353 (National Emergency expands Parliament's power) with Article 360 (no such expansion)

concepts.name: Constitutional Basis and Dr. Ambedkar's Vision for Article 360
key_dimensions: Inspired by Section 6 of the American Constitution and the German Weimar Republic's emergency provisions
Dr. Ambedkar explained in the Constituent Assembly that Article 360 was to ensure financial integrity when states jeopardise national finances
Original intent: To deal with situations where a State's fiscal mismanagement threatens the creditworthiness of India as a whole
Debate in Constituent Assembly on whether the provision gave too much power to the Centre — T.T. Krishnamachari's concerns
